question: Which body system uses chemical messengers (hormones) to drive all the body changes during puberty?

options.A: The lymphatic system
options.B: The nervous reflex arc
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The digestive enzyme network

explanation: Spot on! The endocrine system is our body's hormone-manufacturing network, releasing chemical messengers straight into the bloodstream to spark growth and development.

question: How does evaluation differ from routine monitoring in health programmes?

options.A: Evaluation is only performed before the project begins
options.B: Monitoring is done exclusively by government ministers
options.C: Evaluation measures long-term outcomes and overall impact
options.D: Monitoring focuses strictly on community financial budgets

explanation: You've got this! Monitoring tracks daily work, while evaluation looks at the big picture to see if the overall health goals were finally met.

question: Which of these is a common situation that can lead to asphyxia?

options.A: Consuming too much salty food
options.B: Confinement in an airtight space
options.C: Sudden loss of blood from a wound
options.D: A mild viral throat infection

explanation: Being trapped in a tiny, unventilated box or room quickly uses up all the oxygen, leading to suffocation. Always keep safety in mind!

question: What is a likely result of poor integration between different levels of hospital objectives?

options.A: Increased funding from international health organizations
options.B: Better teamwork between doctors and cleaning staff
options.C: Higher patient satisfaction and faster healing times
options.D: Staff frustration and conflicting daily priorities

explanation: When goals contradict each other across levels, workers do not know what to prioritize, leading to confusion and burnout. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h6)

question: What would happen if the articular cartilage at the ends of your bones wore away completely?

options.A: The joint would produce too much fluid and swell instantly
options.B: The joint would lock permanently straight
options.C: Muscles would immediately lose their ability to contract
options.D: Bone surfaces would grind directly against each other, causing pain

explanation: Spot on! Cartilage is a smooth shock absorber. Without it, bare bones rub together, causing the pain and stiffness we see in arthritis.

question: Why do we carry an antiseptic solution like chlorhexidine in the infection prevention pack?

options.A: To act as an energy drink for tired mothers in labor
options.B: To serve as a nice jelly for easing dryness
options.C: To clean and prep the skin before exams or procedures
options.D: To quickly wipe down and clean rusty metal scissors

explanation: Antiseptic solutions lower the number of germs on the skin, which protects the mother and baby from nasty infections during delivery.

question: Why do nurses tuck the edges of an oxygen tent firmly under the mattress?

options.A: To anchor the heavy metal frame securely to the bed
options.B: To prevent the loss of the enriched oxygen atmosphere
options.C: To completely block all ambient light from the room
options.D: To keep the pediatric patient from crawling out of bed

explanation: Tucking the plastic sides under the mattress creates a nice seal so the oxygen stays inside with the child instead of leaking out into the room.

question: What is a major use for 5-HT3 receptor antagonists like ondansetron?

options.A: Bacterial gastroenteritis
options.B: Chronic hypertension
options.C: Parkinson's disease tremors
options.D: Chemotherapy-induced nausea

explanation: That's right! Drugs like ondansetron are lifesavers for preventing and treating the heavy nausea caused by cancer treatments and surgeries. You're mastering pharmacology!

question: A public health nurse inspects local drinking water sources and tracks cholera cases in a neighborhood. Which core function is the nurse performing?

options.A: Financial auditing
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Hospital accreditation
options.D: Policy development

explanation: Monitoring health status and investigating health hazards fall directly under the assessment function of public health. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why isn't just coming into contact with an infectious germ always enough to make someone sick?

options.A: The host must also lack sufficient resistance to harbor the pathogen
options.B: Environmental temperatures must reach absolute zero for transmission
options.C: Agents require permission from local health boards to multiply
options.D: Pathogens cannot survive outside of a sterile laboratory setting

explanation: Exactly! An infection only takes hold if the person's body is susceptible and doesn't have the immunity to fight it off. Great clinical thinking!

question: What happens when a researcher makes a Type I error?

options.A: Concluding a treatment works when it actually does not
options.B: Failing to notice that a treatment works when it actually does
options.C: Selecting a sample that is too small to represent the ward
options.D: Calculating the wrong average for patient blood pressures

explanation: Correct! A Type I error is like celebrating a false positive—thinking your new nursing routine helps patients when it really doesn't do anything special.

question: How do the results of an MBO performance review affect the future?

options.A: They feed directly into the planning cycle for the next period
options.B: They replace the need for patient care audits
options.C: They are permanently locked away and never looked at again
options.D: They are used to reduce the hospital training budget

explanation: Lessons learned from evaluating past performance help shape better, more realistic goals for the next MBO cycle. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why do clinics use more than one test (an algorithm) instead of just one rapid test for a positive result?

options.A: To make the testing process longer and more thorough
options.B: To ensure diagnostic accuracy and prevent misdiagnosis
options.C: To use up excess laboratory supplies before they expire
options.D: To comply with insurance billing requirements for hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Running sequential tests confirms initial results so we protect clients from the heavy emotional blow of a false positive.

question: Why must you always check two patient identifiers (like name and hospital number) before giving an injection?

options.A: To check if the patient prefers a specific injection site
options.B: To ensure the right medication goes to the right person
options.C: To speed up the medication documentation process
options.D: To confirm the patient has a clean skin surface

explanation: You got it! Double-checking identifiers is a golden rule in nursing to make sure you never give the right drug to the wrong patient.

question: What skill must a good nursing leader have alongside management abilities?

options.A: Political party affiliation
options.B: Strong clinical acumen
options.C: Advanced legal training
options.D: Full financial control

explanation: To earn the respect of the nursing team, a leader needs to understand real bedside care and know current clinical guidelines inside and out.

question: How does research directly help you practice evidence-based care on the ward?

options.A: It dictates the exact salary scale for nursing staff
options.B: It eliminates all documentation requirements for nurses
options.C: It replaces the need to assess individual patient preferences
options.D: It provides tested proof of which clinical interventions work best

explanation: Correct! Research gives us the reliable facts we need to update our daily ward procedures and get better results for our patients.

question: What major problem prompted the creation of the essential drugs concept?

options.A: Hospitals had too many doctors and not enough clinical space
options.B: Pharmaceutical companies refused to sell medicines to developing nations
options.C: Countries wasted money on redundant drugs while lacking basic treatments
options.D: Patients refused to take any form of modern pharmaceutical care

explanation: Early global health planners noticed limited budgets were being squandered on ineffective remedies instead of life-saving basics. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: A clinic manager wants to hike drug prices to build a staff canteen. Why does this break DRF rules?

options.A: Staff canteens are illegal in public hospitals
options.B: Drug prices are fixed permanently by international law
options.C: DRF funds must be reinvested strictly into drug procurement and facility operations linked to the fund
options.D: Only the federal government can adjust drug prices

explanation: Think of DRF money as sacred! It's ring-fenced strictly for buying more lifesaving medicines, not for building canteens or other unrelated projects.

question: A nurse believes a new wound dressing heals ulcers faster. What represents the alternative hypothesis?

options.A: Ulcer healing speed is entirely random and cannot be studied
options.B: Both dressings perform with the exact same level of success
options.C: The new dressing has zero impact on how fast ulcers heal
options.D: The new dressing heals ulcers faster than the standard dressing

explanation: You got it! The alternative hypothesis is simply what the researcher expects to happen—in this case, that the new dressing works better.

question: Which type of cancer starts in the bone marrow and doesn't form solid lumps or tumors?

options.A: Melanoma
options.B: Sarcoma
options.C: Leukemia
options.D: Carcinoma

explanation: Leukemia affects our blood-forming tissues, sending lots of abnormal white blood cells into circulation instead of forming a solid tumor.

question: How do migrating cancer cells manage to break into nearby blood vessels?

options.A: They secrete enzymes that break down surrounding tissue barriers
options.B: They attract white blood cells to carry them into circulation
options.C: They wait for the blood vessel walls to rupture from high pressure
options.D: They shrink in size until they slip through normal cell walls

explanation: Spot on! Cancer cells release special chemical enzymes that chew through tissue barriers and blood vessel walls, letting them slip right into circulation.

question: What is the main difference in how drug treatment is chosen for type 1 versus type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Type 1 is managed strictly through lifestyle changes without drugs
options.B: Type 2 patients never need insulin under any clinical circumstances
options.C: Type 2 can only be treated with injectable non-insulin medications
options.D: Type 1 always requires insulin, while type 2 often starts with oral agents

explanation: Well done! Because type 1 diabetes means the body doesn't make insulin at all, replacement therapy is needed right from the start.

question: What happens to a patient's metabolic rate during severe physiological stress like major trauma or sepsis?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged
options.B: It fluctuates only during sleep
options.C: It drops to zero instantly
options.D: It increases significantly

explanation: Severe physical trauma and infections trigger a hypermetabolic state that dramatically increases energy expenditure. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h7)

question: You visit a woman at 32 weeks who suddenly starts heavy vaginal bleeding. What should be your very first action?

options.A: Wait for her husband to return from work before acting
options.B: Tell her to rest until morning and monitor her
options.C: Ask her to walk around to encourage blood flow
options.D: Stabilize her condition and initiate emergency transport

explanation: Heavy bleeding late in pregnancy is a major emergency. Stabilize her as best as you can and get her moving to the hospital right away!

question: Which lobe houses the primary auditory cortex?

options.A: Parietal lobe
options.B: Temporal lobe
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The superior part of the temporal lobe is dedicated to receiving and processing auditory information. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h4)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the popular BRAIDED counseling mnemonic?

options.A: Billing
options.B: Bandage
options.C: Bedrest
options.D: Benefits

explanation: In contraceptive counseling, the BRAIDED framework reminds nurses to discuss benefits, risks, alternatives, and other key details with the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: What happens to the marks on daily tally sheets at the end of a clinic day?

options.A: The marks are counted and transferred into monthly summary registers
options.B: The tally marks are erased so the sheet can be reused tomorrow
options.C: The papers are burned to protect patient confidentiality
options.D: The sheets are mailed directly to the international health organization

explanation: Spot on! At the end of the day, we count up the tally marks so they can feed into our bigger monthly summary books and reports.

question: Why is it important to ask patients if they have visited patent medicine vendors when taking their history?

options.A: Hospital records automatically track all purchases made in private shops
options.B: Many informal vendors administer unsterile injections that patients forget to mention
options.C: Patent medicine vendors are legally required to report side effects
options.D: Patients only get infections when visiting registered general hospitals

explanation: Patients often think of informal drug purchases as casual and might forget to mention them. Asking directly helps us catch hidden risks like unsterile shots!

question: Which category do single-use items like gauze and disposable syringes fall under?

options.A: Emergency pharmaceuticals
options.B: Durable equipment
options.C: Consumables
options.D: Controlled substances

explanation: Consumables are those handy everyday items designed to be used just once for a patient and then safely discarded.

question: Why must safety measures respect a patient's independence?

options.A: Patients will ignore rules that make them feel helpless
options.B: Families prefer not to assist elderly relatives
options.C: Independent patients recover faster from surgery
options.D: Hospital policies demand self-care routines

explanation: If safety rules take away all freedom, patients often try to bypass them secretly, which actually increases their risk of accidents. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h1)

question: What time of day is best for taking a patient's daily weight to get a reliable comparison?

options.A: Immediately after a large dinner
options.B: Late in the evening before sleep
options.C: In the morning after voiding
options.D: Right after finishing afternoon tea

explanation: Weighing in the morning after the bladder is emptied helps avoid the changes in weight caused by food and fluids taken throughout the day.

question: Why might a standard X-ray appear completely normal during the very first week of acute osteomyelitis?

options.A: X-rays cannot pass through calcium deposits in the human skeleton
options.B: Early bacterial infections only attack the blood and never the bone tissue
options.C: Significant bone destruction must occur before it becomes visible on an X-ray
options.D: Radiation from the X-ray machine temporarily hides early bone changes

explanation: Standard X-rays require about 30 to 50 percent bone matrix loss before changes show up, meaning early infection is often missed on plain films. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h6)

question: What makes a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) so great for a busy rural health clinic?

options.A: It gives quick results from a finger-prick blood sample without complex equipment
options.B: It permanently prevents future mosquito bites from causing infection
options.C: It is the only test capable of identifying dead parasites after treatment
options.D: It tells the nurse the exact number of parasites circulating in the blood

explanation: Spot on! RDTs are fast, portable, and a lifesaver in clinics where there are no fancy lab machines or steady electricity.

question: What is the main benefit of using a person-centred approach in post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It helps match birth control to the client's unique lifestyle and goals
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never feel any grief
options.C: It speeds up the clinic discharge paperwork
options.D: It forces the client to choose the strongest long-term method

explanation: Person-centred care is all about listening to what the patient wants. When they choose a method that fits their life, they are much happier using it!

question: What is the primary public health way to prevent iodine deficiency in a population?

options.A: Providing Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food packets
options.B: Distributing high-dose vitamin A capsules
options.C: Promoting the universal use of iodized salt
options.D: Administering iron-folate tablets to infants

explanation: Correct! Iodized salt is the simplest, most effective way to reach everyone and stop conditions like goiter from developing.

question: How do hookworm larvae usually enter the human body?

options.A: Bites from infected mosquitoes
options.B: Drinking unboiled river water
options.C: Direct penetration through the skin
options.D: Inhalation of airborne dust particles

explanation: Hookworm larvae love hanging out in contaminated soil. When people walk barefoot, these tiny worms can actually burrow right through the skin. Good reason to wear sandals!

question: A lack of which vital nutrient in early pregnancy is linked to neural tube defects like spina bifida?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Potassium

explanation: Folic acid is a hero vitamin! It helps the neural tube close properly in the first weeks of pregnancy, keeping baby safe from conditions like spina bifida.

question: Which cells in your body carry MHC Class I molecules on their surface?

options.A: Only mature red blood cells
options.B: Almost all nucleated cells
options.C: Only free-floating antibodies
options.D: Only uninfected skin cells

explanation: Nearly every cell with a nucleus wears MHC Class I proteins like an ID badge to show whether it is healthy or infected from within.

question: What does it mean when a Drug Revolving Fund is described as 'ring-fenced'?

options.A: The pharmacy door must be locked with a special metal ring
options.B: Drugs are arranged in circular shelves inside the store
options.C: Profits are shared equally among all clinical department heads
options.D: Money from drug sales is kept separate and used only to buy more drugs

explanation: Ring-fencing is like putting a protective fence around the money. It ensures drug funds aren't mistakenly used to pay for other hospital bills!

question: A newborn is diagnosed with anencephaly. Which part of the embryo's neural tube failed to close?

options.A: Caudal spinal cord
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Anterior neuropore
options.D: Posterior neuropore

explanation: You got it! Anencephaly happens when the top end (anterior neuropore) of the neural tube doesn't close properly, affecting brain development.

question: Why must body tissues and human parts be separated from normal general waste?

options.A: Pathological waste can be sold easily to local recycling companies
options.B: Pathological waste weighs much less than normal office paper
options.C: General waste bins are designed to dissolve organic tissues rapidly
options.D: Pathological waste requires specialized treatment due to human tissue contents

explanation: Well done! Human tissues need special, respectful disposal to prevent disease spread and public health risks.

question: Which of the following complications is strongly linked to poor nutritional status in bedridden patients?

options.A: Ear infections
options.B: Kidney stones
options.C: Vision loss
options.D: Pressure injuries

explanation: Malnourished tissue breaks down much faster under pressure, making pressure injuries very common in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse can do to treat a genetic degenerative disorder?

options.A: Evaluating bowel patterns to prevent severe constipation
options.B: Administering a daily cure to reverse genetic mutations
options.C: Assessing respiratory effort and cough strength regularly
options.D: Monitoring skin integrity for signs of pressure injury

explanation: Right now, we can't rewrite someone's DNA. Our nursing care focuses completely on keeping them comfortable and preventing complications.

question: How are parents viewed within the framework of family-centered home care?

options.A: As passive observers during medical treatments
options.B: As temporary assistants to the visiting nurse
options.C: As essential frontline providers of daily care
options.D: As secondary sources of medical information

explanation: Exactly! Parents are the ones handling daily care between nurse visits, making them absolute VIPs on the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h2)

question: A resident needs physical help to cut their food and bring it to their mouth. Which daily living activity does this fall under?

options.A: Bathing
options.B: Feeding
options.C: Transferring
options.D: Toileting

explanation: Well done! Eating and drinking assistance is classified under the feeding category of ADLs.

question: Where should you place the sticky AED pads on an adult patient's chest?

options.A: Right upper chest and left lower ribcage
options.B: Upper back and lower abdomen
options.C: Directly over the center of the breastbone
options.D: Both shoulders near the outer collarbones

explanation: Placing one pad on the upper right chest and the other on the lower left side creates a diagonal path so the shock travels right through the heart muscle.

question: A patient gets a wound infection after a nurse uses an uncleaned blood pressure cuff. What kind of spread is this?

options.A: Direct transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Indirect transmission via a fomite

explanation: Great job! The uncleaned cuff acts as a fomite, carrying the germ indirectly from one patient to the next.

question: What is a key job of interneurons in a reflex pathway?

options.A: To physically contract the target organ
options.B: To distribute signals to multiple destinations like muscles and the brain
options.C: To act as primary sensory receptors in the skin
options.D: To generate the initial physical stimulus for the body

explanation: Interneurons help sort and share the message, making sure your muscles react quickly while also sending a quick heads-up note to your brain!

question: What is the main feature of a correlational study?

options.A: Variables are not manipulated by the researcher
options.B: Random assignment is used for all participants
options.C: A specific medication is tested on patients
options.D: Only laboratory animals are studied

explanation: Spot on! In correlational studies, we simply observe natural relationships without changing or controlling things ourselves. You've got this!

question: What does the practice of evidence-based nursing combine?

options.A: Traditional beliefs, trial and error, and personal opinions
options.B: Hospital policies, doctor preferences, and budget limits
options.C: Quick solutions, strict punishments, and administrative orders
options.D: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values

explanation: Evidence-based practice merges scientific research, the nurse's professional judgment, and what matters most to the individual patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the term for dilated veins in the scrotum that can negatively affect sperm production?

options.A: Orchitis
options.B: A varicocele
options.C: Hydrocele
options.D: Cryptorchidism

explanation: A varicocele involves swollen scrotal veins that increase local temperature, which often interferes with normal spermatogenesis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which complaint from a pregnant patient should make you suspect her brain is being affected by preeclampsia?

options.A: Frequent swollen ankles
options.B: Increased appetite
options.C: Mild lower backache
options.D: A stubborn frontal headache

explanation: A headache that just won't go away—especially if her vision also gets blurry—is a classic warning sign that her brain is reacting to high blood pressure.

question: What is the primary job of an Institutional Review Board (IRB)?

options.A: Securing big money grants for labs
options.B: Writing nursing textbooks
options.C: Marketing new drugs to hospitals
options.D: Protecting the rights and safety of human research participants

explanation: Spot on! The IRB acts as a safety shield to ensure human subjects are treated ethically and safely.

question: How does restrictive cardiomyopathy mainly affect the heart?

options.A: It thins out the walls until the heart bursts.
options.B: It makes the muscle rigid, preventing normal ventricular filling.
options.C: It causes the heart valves to dissolve rapidly.
options.D: It speeds up the electrical conduction pathways permanently.

explanation: In restrictive cardiomyopathy, the heart muscle becomes stiff and rigid. Because it can't relax, the chambers struggle to fill up with blood.

question: What is the double nutritional challenge facing the Nigerian healthcare system today?

options.A: Complete absence of nutritional disorders in urban and rural areas
options.B: Only severe protein deficiency with zero cases of chronic illness
options.C: Strictly overnutrition and obesity with no forms of hunger
options.D: Dealing with undernutrition while also seeing a rise in chronic lifestyle diseases

explanation: Nigeria faces a double burden: fighting traditional issues like hunger and malnutrition while also managing lifestyle illnesses like diabetes and high blood pressure.

question: A newly registered pregnant woman is diagnosed with HIV at her first clinic visit. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to terminate the pregnancy to protect her health.
options.B: Start her on lifelong antiretroviral therapy immediately.
options.C: Wait until her second trimester before prescribing any medications.
options.D: Delay treatment until her CD4 cell count drops below 200.

explanation: Current guidelines recommend prompt initiation of ART for all pregnant women living with HIV, regardless of clinical stage or CD4 count. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: Where do bedside nurses usually spot their first research ideas?

options.A: By reading financial audits of hospital pharmacies
options.B: Through political debates in national assemblies
options.C: Inside historical textbooks written decades ago
options.D: During routine patient care observations and shift routines

explanation: As nurses, we see what happens on the ward every single day. Your daily clinical experiences are a goldmine for research topics!

question: What is the main goal of keeping a patient clean and fresh?

options.A: To shorten the hospital stay
options.B: To protect skin and stop infections
options.C: To cover up unpleasant room smells
options.D: To boost body metabolism

explanation: Well done! Keeping skin clean stops it from breaking down and keeps out harmful germs. You've got this!

question: Why does the surface of the brain have so many folds and grooves?

options.A: To improve the circulation of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: To increase the surface area for more neurons
options.C: To separate the left and right sides of the body
options.D: To absorb physical shock from head injuries

explanation: Folding packs a massive amount of brain power into a small space, giving us room for lots of nerve cells!

question: Where is the normal point of maximal impulse (PMI) located on a healthy adult chest?

options.A: Second intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: Third intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: Seventh intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
options.D: Fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line

explanation: You'll usually find the normal PMI right at the fifth intercostal space along the left midclavicular line. Excellent clinical landmark! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which joint is most likely to suffer first when a patient has a sudden gout attack?

options.A: The hip joint
options.B: The elbow joint
options.C: The shoulder joint
options.D: The big toe

explanation: Great job! The base of the big toe is the classic hotspot for a first-time gout attack. Because of cooler body temperatures there and normal daily pressure, uric acid loves to form crystals in this spot first.

question: What happens during qualitative data analysis?

options.A: Patients fill out numerical rating scales for pain
options.B: Computers calculate complex algebraic formulas and p-values
options.C: Researchers code text to identify recurring themes and patterns
options.D: Blood samples are centrifuged in a hospital laboratory

explanation: Qualitative analysis organizes narrative words and interviews into meaningful categories or themes. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h6)

question: A client refuses a specific birth control method due to local community rumors. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Refuse to provide any further healthcare services to the client
options.B: Listen respectfully and provide accurate education to clear up the rumors
options.C: Dismiss the client's worries as silly and push the method anyway
options.D: Tell the client that community opinions should never matter

explanation: Respectful listening combined with gentle, accurate education helps address fears rooted in social stigma and community misconceptions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic example of indirect transmission via a fomite?

options.A: Catching an infection after touching a contaminated door handle
options.B: Getting malaria from a mosquito bite
options.C: Contracting a sexually transmitted infection through direct contact
options.D: Inhaling large droplets expelled during a close-range sneeze

explanation: A 'fomite' is just a fancy word for any non-living object—like a door handle, phone, or pen—that carries germs from one person to another.

question: What is a big perk of the newer, single-size silicone diaphragms?

options.A: They can be left in place inside the vagina for up to a week
options.B: They do not require an internal pelvic exam for professional sizing
options.C: They completely eliminate the need to use spermicide creams
options.D: They provide full protection against all sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Universal single-size diaphragms are a lifesaver because one standard size fits most women, saving them from a traditional fitting exam.

question: Why is proper healthcare waste management considered a key infection control practice?

options.A: It prevents the spread of harmful microorganisms found in discarded items
options.B: It speeds up the process of discharging stable patients from the ward
options.C: It lowers the monthly electricity and water utility bills of the facility
options.D: It ensures the hospital compounds look neat and presentable to visitors

explanation: Spot on! Discarded medical materials often carry germs that can multiply and spread infections if we don't handle them right. You're doing great!

question: A local clinic plans to administer 4,000 curative injections over the next quarter without a waste factor. If each injection needs one syringe, how many syringes should be ordered?
explanation: Multiplying the total injection encounters by the dose per encounter without a waste factor gives the exact baseline total of 4,000. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is pregnancy particularly tough on a teenage bride's physical body?

options.A: Her body is still growing and competes with the fetus for nutrients
options.B: Adult nutritional requirements no longer apply to her body
options.C: Her immune system completely shuts down during gestation
options.D: Hormonal changes stop her bones from ever healing properly

explanation: Teenagers are still growing themselves! Their bodies need nutrients for their own development, which creates a direct competition with the growing baby.

question: What primary category of life does water microbiology study?

options.A: Chemical pollutants in rivers
options.B: Microscopic organisms found in water
options.C: Large aquatic plants and fish
options.D: Mineral deposits in borehole pipes

explanation: Water microbiology focuses strictly on the tiny living forms like bacteria, viruses, and protozoa present in water systems. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h1)

question: A nurse notices that a patient's skin is very dry and lacks normal turgor. Which physiological issue does this most likely suggest?

options.A: Dehydration and fluid volume deficit
options.B: Excessive vitamin D production
options.C: Normal localized blood pooling
options.D: High levels of subcutaneous fat

explanation: Poor skin turgor and dryness are classic clinical signs of fluid loss and dehydration. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)

question: Which post-WWII law provided funding for hospital construction and indirectly led to the growth of nursing homes?

options.A: The Social Security Amendment
options.B: The Medicare and Medicaid Act
options.C: The Nursing Home Reform Act
options.D: The Hill-Burton Act

explanation: The Hill-Burton Act funded a massive wave of hospital building. Once those hospitals started discharging patients who still needed long-term care, the need for separate nursing homes became super obvious!

question: Which clinical condition is most likely to produce a weak, thready pulse?

options.A: Severe dehydration and fluid loss
options.B: Heavy physical exercise at the gym
options.C: Sudden fright or emotional excitement
options.D: Mild fever from a viral throat infection

explanation: Dehydration lowers blood volume, resulting in a weak, thready pulse that is difficult to feel clearly. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why should you never point a used sharp device toward your own body?

options.A: It causes the medication inside to evaporate quickly
options.B: It makes the needle dull for future patients
options.C: It increases the chance of a direct puncture injury
options.D: It violates hospital rules regarding uniform neatness

explanation: Keep sharp points facing away from you so that if your hand slips, you won't get poked.

question: Which of the following is a potential challenge nurses must watch out for when using digital dietary counselling?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever speaking to a doctor again
options.B: It is illegal to discuss food choices over a video call
options.C: It automatically makes all patients instantly lose weight
options.D: Some patients may struggle with technology or lack internet access

explanation: Digital divides are real; older adults or low-income clients may lack the devices or skills needed for video visits. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h7)

question: What does a high-pressure alarm on a mechanical ventilator usually mean?

options.A: The breathing tube has fallen out entirely
options.B: The patient's body temperature has suddenly dropped
options.C: There is a blockage or kink in the airway tubing
options.D: The hospital oxygen tank is completely empty

explanation: High-pressure alarms sound when the ventilator hits resistance trying to push air in—often due to secretions, a mucus plug, or the patient biting the tube. Spot on!

question: What does "interdependence" mean in a community?

options.A: The government controls every aspect of private family life
options.B: Members and subgroups rely on each other for survival and support
options.C: Foreign countries manage all local health clinics
options.D: Every single household produces all its own food and medicine

explanation: Interdependence means people and groups lean on one another to make daily life work smoothly.

question: Which way of spreading germs involves tiny particles floating in the air over long distances?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Direct contact transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Droplet spread transmission

explanation: Airborne transmission happens when tiny germs ride on air currents and stay suspended long enough to be breathed in by someone else.

question: Why are regular joint simulation drills important before a disaster happens?

options.A: They replace the need for community involvement in healthcare delivery
options.B: They allow agencies to practice working together and find plan flaws
options.C: They guarantee that natural disasters will completely bypass the region
options.D: They reduce the annual budgetary allocation required for security forces

explanation: Practice makes perfect! Simulations let different teams test their teamwork and fix mistakes before a real emergency occurs.

question: What is the very first sign a nurse looks for on a growth chart to spot growth faltering?

options.A: A stable horizontal line that matches the birth weight
options.B: A sudden spike in height above the ninety-fifth percentile
options.C: A flattening or downward crossing of weight percentiles
options.D: An abrupt increase in head circumference beyond normal limits

explanation: Growth faltering happens quietly at first—the child stops gaining weight along their usual curve, causing the line to flatten or dip across the percentile tracks.

question: What does a spiritual assessment in palliative care mostly focus on?

options.A: Memorization of sacred religious texts
options.B: Meaning, purpose, and inner peace
options.C: Regular attendance at local religious services
options.D: Donations made to charitable organizations

explanation: Spirituality isn't just about religion—it's about helping a patient find hope, peace, and meaning in their journey.

question: Which group usually faces the hardest time moving to safety during an emergency evacuation?

options.A: Elderly individuals and people with disabilities
options.B: Young adults with personal cars
options.C: Trained rescue personnel
options.D: Government officials in the capital city

explanation: Older people and those with physical challenges often struggle to move quickly or hear alerts during a rush. Every little bit of practice counts!

question: What is the primary male sex hormone responsible for secondary sex characteristics?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Aldosterone

explanation: Testosterone is made mainly by the testes. It drives male reproductive development, muscle building, and masculine physical traits.

question: Which of the following symptoms should a nurse instruct a client to report immediately as a red-flag warning?

options.A: Sudden severe pelvic pain or excessive bleeding
options.B: Mild fatigue after completing a normal workday
options.C: Minor bloating before the onset of menses
options.D: Slight breast tenderness during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Sudden severe pain or hemorrhage can indicate acute surgical emergencies like a ruptured cyst, ectopic pregnancy, or severe post-op bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h8)

question: Which hormone triggers the release of stored energy when the body is fasting?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Gastrin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Glucagon

explanation: You're doing brilliant! When blood sugar dips during a fast, glucagon steps up to say, 'Time to release our stored energy reserves!'

question: How do sensory areas and association areas work together?

options.A: Sensory areas control muscles while association areas block pain
options.B: Sensory areas register raw data while association areas give it meaning
options.C: Sensory areas interpret complex thoughts while association areas detect light
options.D: Sensory areas store memories while association areas process movement

explanation: The primary sensory cortex receives the basic sensation, and the adjacent association areas analyze and interpret what that sensation actually means. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the primary function of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Filter waste products from the blood
options.B: Produce, sustain, and transport sperm
options.C: Digest complex dietary proteins
options.D: Regulate total body water balance

explanation: The primary role of the male reproductive system is the creation and delivery of sperm cells for reproduction alongside hormone production. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: What indicates a successful outcome for a resident leaving a half-way house?

options.A: An inability to manage basic finances without supervision
options.B: The ability to maintain stability and live independently
options.C: The permanent loss of all contact with family members
options.D: A court order requiring them to return to hospital wards

explanation: You're doing great! Success means the resident can handle everyday life, look after their health, and thrive outside structured care.

question: Why is knowing the exact route abbreviation so important for safe medication delivery?

options.A: It determines how fast the drug works and prevents wrong-route errors
options.B: It replaces the need to check the patient's identity band
options.C: It decides which nurse is legally permitted to touch the patient
options.D: It tells the nurse the exact financial cost of the medication supply

explanation: Spot on! Different routes change how quickly a drug enters the bloodstream. Getting the route wrong can lead to serious patient harm, so always double-check!

question: A nurse wants to test if a new wound dressing heals ulcers faster. What would be the alternative hypothesis?

options.A: The new dressing has no effect on ulcer healing time
options.B: Ulcer healing is entirely unrelated to dressings
options.C: All dressings heal ulcers at the exact same rate
options.D: The new dressing changes the healing time of ulcers

explanation: The alternative hypothesis is what you actually suspect will happen—that there is a real difference or relationship!

question: Why are nurses so important when pregnant women come in for prenatal services?

options.A: They are legally required to perform all surgical procedures during birth
options.B: They prescribe all medications independently of medical doctors
options.C: They diagnose genetic disorders without needing laboratory equipment
options.D: They serve as the primary contact to build trust and encourage hospital deliveries

explanation: You are often the very first person she talks to! Building that warm, trusting relationship makes her feel safe and much more likely to come back for a safe hospital delivery.

question: A 5-year-old child with a heavy roundworm infection has vomiting, colicky tummy pain, and a sausage-like lump felt in the belly. What is the most likely complication?

options.A: Acute glomerulonephritis
options.B: Intestinal obstruction
options.C: Hepatic abscess
options.D: Pulmonary embolism

explanation: A tangled mass of worms can physically block the small bowel, causing severe pain, vomiting, and a noticeable mass.

question: What is the typical acid-base blood gas state during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Acute metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Uncompensated metabolic acidosis
options.C: Severe respiratory acidosis
options.D: Compensated respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Mums breathe off extra carbon dioxide, leading to mild respiratory alkalosis which the kidneys smoothly balance out with bicarbonate. Great revision!

question: How does a mild fever actually help your body fight an infection?

options.A: It stops the heart from pumping blood to sick tissues.
options.B: It flushes germs out entirely through the sweat glands.
options.C: It speeds up metabolism and helps white blood cells work better.
options.D: it melts the cell walls of harmful bacteria directly.

explanation: A controlled fever creates a hostile environment for germs while boosting your immune cells so they can do their job faster!

question: If an air ring is specially ordered for a patient, what is the correct way to prepare it?

options.A: Place it directly against bare skin without any cover
options.B: Inflate it to maximum capacity for firm support
options.C: Fill it with warm water instead of air
options.D: Inflate it only slightly and cover it with a soft sheet

explanation: Spot on! Inflating it just a little bit keeps hard edges from digging into the skin, and a clean cover adds an extra layer of comfort.

question: What is the main job of the epididymis in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Storage and maturation of sperm
options.B: Production of testosterone
options.C: Secretion of thick mucus
options.D: Filtration of blood waste

explanation: You've got this! Sperm are made in the testes, but they hang out in the epididymis to grow up and learn how to swim properly before they are released.

question: Which type of budget covers long-term investments and big purchases like a new X-ray machine?

options.A: Personnel budget
options.B: Cash flow budget
options.C: Capital budget
options.D: Operating budget

explanation: Capital budgets are for the big-ticket items—like heavy machinery and building upgrades—that stay with the hospital for many years.

question: What early signs do women with ovarian cancer most often report to their doctors?

options.A: High fever, chills, and purulent vaginal discharge
options.B: Sudden, sharp, localized stabbing pain in the right lower quadrant
options.C: Painful urination and visible blood in the urine
options.D: Vague digestive changes, bloating, and early fullness when eating

explanation: Good job! These symptoms can easily feel like a normal tummy upset, which is why early detection is tricky.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical role of the nurse during the implementation phase?

options.A: Motivating volunteers when the work gets difficult
options.B: Coordinating activities between different groups
options.C: Acting as a strict dictator who punishes lazy workers
options.D: Providing technical advice on health procedures

explanation: Nurses act as facilitators, advisors, and motivators, not as authoritarian bosses who punish community members. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h6)

question: A patient with severe amoebiasis suddenly gets a rigid, board-like tummy and severe pain all over. What is your primary worry as a nurse?

options.A: Normal recovery after medication
options.B: Temporary gas accumulation
options.C: Bowel perforation and peritonitis
options.D: A mild medication side effect

explanation: Spot on! A rigid abdomen is a classic red flag for peritonitis caused by a perforated bowel. Quick action is life-saving!

question: How is a 'near miss' different from an adverse event?

options.A: A near miss is caught before reaching the patient, causing no actual harm
options.B: An adverse event never involves medication or treatment mistakes
options.C: An adverse event is only recorded if the patient complains publicly
options.D: A near miss always results in permanent physical disability

explanation: Well done! A near miss is a close call where a mistake almost happened or reached the patient, but was caught in time so nobody got hurt.

question: Why are metabolic and endocrine disorders considered such a big deal for public health?

options.A: They only affect elderly populations in rural areas
options.B: They are easily cured with a single antibiotic
options.C: They cause widespread and systemic complications
options.D: They never require long-term medical management

explanation: Because our hormones control so many different body systems, when something goes wrong here, it affects the whole body. Great thinking!

question: Which lymphoid organ is primarily responsible for filtering blood and destroying old red blood cells?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Thymus
options.C: Liver
options.D: Tonsil

explanation: The spleen filters blood, recycles iron from hemoglobin, and removes damaged red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why do health NGOs often experience high staff turnover?

options.A: Clinics close down every few months due to weather
options.B: Staff members are legally required to change jobs yearly
options.C: They often rely on short-term contracts and lower pay
options.D: Government hospitals steal all qualified nurses by force

explanation: That's right! Because funding comes in short bursts, NGOs often can't offer permanent jobs with great pay, so staff look for stable work elsewhere. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h5)

question: A woman with sickle cell disease is admitted in active labor. What is the most critical nursing action for her care?

options.A: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.B: Encouraging unmedicated natural childbirth at home
options.C: Maintaining strict intravenous hydration
options.D: Keeping the room temperature cold to prevent shivering

explanation: Spot on! Dehydration makes the blood thicker and can easily trigger a crisis, so keeping fluids flowing through an IV is an absolute must.

question: What is another name commonly given to the enteric nervous system?

options.A: The central coordinator
options.B: The second brain
options.C: The vagal network
options.D: The sympathetic trunk

explanation: The enteric nervous system is often called the second brain because it contains a vast network of neurons that can control digestive functions independently of the brain. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h1)

question: What do we call the ability of an antigen to actually spark an immune reaction?

options.A: Pathogenicity
options.B: Virulence
options.C: Toxicology
options.D: Immunogenicity

explanation: Break the word down: 'Immuno' for immune system, and 'genicity' for generating a response. You've got this!

question: What is the main way that antiemetic (anti-nausea) drugs stop vomiting?

options.A: Blocking specific neurotransmitter receptors
options.B: Destroying circulating toxins in the blood
options.C: Enhancing gastric motility and emptying
options.D: Increasing blood flow to the medulla oblongata

explanation: You nailed it! Anti-nausea meds work by latching onto and blocking the chemical receptors along the vomiting pathway so the brain doesn't get the 'throw up' signal. Keep it up!

question: How does skeletal traction differ fundamentally from skin traction?

options.A: Skeletal traction avoids any risk of infection because no hardware is used
options.B: Skeletal traction uses much lighter weights for short periods
options.C: Skeletal traction attaches directly to bone using metal pins
options.D: Skeletal traction relies entirely on elastic bandages wrapped loosely

explanation: Skeletal traction requires surgical insertion of pins or wires into the bone to handle heavier weights over a longer duration, unlike skin-surface methods. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for older adults with advanced illnesses?

options.A: Quickly discharging the patient from home care
options.B: Maximizing comfort and quality of life
options.C: Stopping all forms of nursing communication
options.D: Finding a complete cure for every diagnosis

explanation: Palliative care isn't about curing; it's all about easing pain and distressing symptoms so the patient can live their remaining days with dignity and comfort.

question: Which part of the brain is the main bridge between the nervous and endocrine systems?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: That's correct! The hypothalamus acts as the chief coordinator, linking brain signals to hormone control.

question: What does community resource mobilization primarily aim to fix in under-resourced schools?

options.A: Frequent absenteeism among school administrators
options.B: Outdated teacher training certification processes
options.C: Shortages in basic health and physical infrastructure
options.D: Low scores in national mathematics examinations

explanation: Mobilizing local resources directly targets physical gaps like clean water, toilets, and functional sick bays. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h3)

question: What happens to a patient's red blood cells if they are given a severely hypotonic intravenous solution?

options.A: They remain completely unchanged
options.B: They immediately multiply rapidly
options.C: They swell and may burst
options.D: They shrink and shrivel up

explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water rushes into the cells because the surrounding fluid has a lower solute concentration, causing the cells to swell and potentially rupture (lysis). [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why do family members often encourage pregnant women to follow strict local food rules?

options.A: To prevent complications like a baby growing too large for a normal delivery
options.B: To reserve expensive food items exclusively for the village elders
options.C: To ensure the mother maintains a high level of physical fitness
options.D: To comply with modern international nutritional guidelines

explanation: You got it! Most food taboos come from well-meaning family members trying to keep the baby small so delivery will be easier.

question: Why must a food handler with a finger cut wear a brightly colored waterproof bandage?

options.A: To prevent the bandage from absorbing water in the sink
options.B: To make it easily visible if it falls off into the food
options.C: To speed up the healing process of the skin wound
options.D: To hide the injury from customers who might feel uncomfortable

explanation: Bright waterproof plasters make it super easy to spot and retrieve the bandage if it accidentally drops into a meal. Smart, right?

question: When food prices shoot up way past family incomes, what do households usually do first?

options.A: Growing all required food supplies inside the home
options.B: Stopping all food purchases until prices return to normal
options.C: Replacing nutrient-dense foods with cheap carbohydrates
options.D: Increasing the daily consumption of fresh meat and fish

explanation: When money is tight, families switch to cheap filling carbs and cut out expensive proteins and fresh produce. It's a tough economic reality.

question: What should you do if you find a banned or unclear abbreviation on a patient's drug chart?

options.A: Cross it out and rewrite it using personal shorthand codes
options.B: Guess the intended dose based on the patient's age and weight
options.C: Administer the medication immediately to avoid treatment delays
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the drug

explanation: Safety first! Never guess when an order is unclear. Always contact the prescribing doctor or clinician to verify what they meant before giving the medication.

question: When is the best time to bring in palliative care for a patient diagnosed with lymphoma?

options.A: Only during the final 24 hours of life
options.B: Alongside regular curative treatment right from the start
options.C: Only when the patient asks for hospice
options.D: After all chemotherapy options have failed

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for end-of-life; it's about comfort and symptom relief, and it works best when started early alongside cancer treatment!

question: What does the principle of equity mean in mental health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring vulnerable groups have fair access to support
options.B: Allowing only community leaders to make decisions
options.C: Giving the exact same treatment to every single person
options.D: Making sure rich people pay for poor people's drugs

explanation: Equity focuses on fairness and making sure that those who face the greatest disadvantages receive the resources they need to thrive. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h2)

question: As a student nurse doing chest compressions, how do you make sure blood keeps filling the heart between pushes?

options.A: Leaning slightly on the chest to save energy
options.B: Compressing the sternum as deeply as possible
options.C: Allowing full chest recoil after every compression
options.D: Slowing down the compression rate to 60 per minute

explanation: Make sure to lift your weight completely off the chest after each push. This lets blood flow back into the heart chambers ready for the next squeeze!
